Core technology - Dualzone EGD: Wood grain aligned along heel and toe edge in two unbroken zones perpendicular to rest of core for consistent edge hold and strength [7] 55. Laminate: 45° Carbon Highlights — tip-to-tail carbon layer with 45° angled fibres for reduced weight and fine-tuned torsional flex [1][7] 56. Laminate fibre effect: A 45° fiber angle provides a more aggressive ride (vs 60° which is more playful) [1] 57. Fiberglass: Mystery Glass — custom blend of fiberglass and carbon fiber designed to optimize strength-to-weight ratio [14] 58. Fiberglass structure (detailed, forum): 0°/UDG & +/- 45° Stitched, 45° Carbon Highlights [9] 59. Base material: Sintered WFO (extra absorbent, high density sintered material infused with specially formulated wax) [1][7] 60. Resin: Super Sap® Epoxy — bio-based materials that reduce carbon footprint by 50% over conventional petroleum-based epoxies [1] 61. Factory treatment: Infinite Ride™ (overbuilt and machine-broken-in for consistent performance from day 1) [1] 62. Sidewall technology: Slimrail slanted sidewalls (reduces thickness and weight) [25] 63. Forestry certification: FSC™ Certified core woods [15] 64. Mounting system: The Split Channel (with channel compatible pre-mounted pucks) [1][7] 65. Binding compatibility: Compatible with all major bindings, not just Burton's [1] 66. Pre-mounted pucks: Yes, comes with binding pucks ready to go [6] 67. Recommended binding: Burton Step On Splitboard Binding (reviewer's favorite for touring) [6] 68. Skin compatibility note: Works best with Burton proprietary skins due to swallowtail shape [6] 69. Splitboard function: Splits into two separate halves for touring/uphill travel with climbing skins; special splitboard bindings required [8] 70. Powder float: Exceptional — "Unsinkable" per Backcountry Magazine Tahoe tester [23] 115. Surfy feel: "It really felt surfy in the best possible way" [6] 116. Tree riding: Reviewer's favorite board for jamming through trees [24] 117. Turn initiation: Instantaneous short-to-medium turns from sidecut and spoon-shaped nose [23] 118. Pop and response: Board almost pops back as you go in and out of turns [26] 121. Maneuverability: Unique maneuverability in the splitboard category [26] 122. Hard-pack performance: Not at home in steep, hard conditions [6] 127. Firm snow nose catch: Nose feels a tad catchy when maneuvering in firm snow [6] 128.
